summary: Preserve the inherited head, including its Russian editorial question about splitting roots; this evidence alone does not settle etymological homonymy. Do not join the meal verb to mʕr on the basis of a consonant-only form.

Physical fit has the fitting entity as subject and the containing space as b-/ʕal-phrase or l-suffix: ḥa ənsan fits into a fronted cell resumed by -la (11/123). The German cell-has-room paraphrase reverses that perspective. The yoke example similarly has bulls as contained subjects.

The emotional token 61/43 has masculine zʕuro but feminine/default ʕaryo plus b gawe. It supports an internal experiencer construction; it does not show simple subject agreement with the young man. No new emotional sense is created from this one already quoted token.
koʕəryo ebe w lə=kʕəryo ebe at 93/29 is one marginal-capacity statement, rendered kaum eben by the edition. Two occurrence decisions are required, but a single example suffices.

III meal forms take L-series Preterit agents yet need no object. Food may be stated as an unmarked noun list, and companions/food sources may occur with ʕam/ʕal. Habitual workshop lunch contrasts with an irrealis recurrent wish in the existing Infectum-wa box.

III.1 hineinbringen has only the figurative word-into-head example here. Do not widen it to a separately asserted mental-acceptance sense or claim unattested literal motion; the inherited gloss remains.
The 76/64 translation correction is grammatical: second-person plural aʕmayxu must be you. No translation is generated for any new example; added quotations retain edition wording and language.

Should the emotional endurance construction at 61/43 be analysed with a default feminine situation subject and an experiencer b gawe, or as another noncanonical agreement pattern? Confirm with a native speaker.
Do the physical-fit, endurance and stem-III lunch items require separate homonymous roots as the inherited head asks? This corpus demonstrates different constructions, not their etymological history.
For 98/49, verify the final Ṭrowe command and translation alignment before any new full-verse quotation. The existing mental-insertion example is kept, without quoting the flagged translation anew.
Confirm whether I.1b expresses fitting/capacity rather than entry as motion in the tunnel/recess contexts. Explicit əzzele beside ʕorele at 66/334 favours distinguishing going from having room.

Spatial subjects include people, a hand, bulls, melons, stoves and measured grain. Containers/supports take b-, a locative l-suffix or ʕal-. Participant and preposition variation does not require one sense per object.
The king not fitting within his own skin is a figurative container construction for agitation, not evidence for a separate physical motion or emotional-transitive sense.
